questions.question: A* search is guaranteed to return the optimal path if the heuristic function h(n) is admissible.
questions.explanation: True. Admissibility guarantees optimal tree search by never overestimating cost to goal.

questions.question: The XOR function can be solved by a single-layer perceptron without hidden layers.
questions.explanation: False. XOR is not linearly separable and requires at least one non-linear hidden layer.

questions.question: ReLU activation avoids the vanishing gradient problem for positive inputs because its derivative is constant 1.0.
questions.explanation: True. For z > 0, d(ReLU)/dz = 1.0, preserving gradient magnitude through deep layers.

questions.question: Convolutional layers share weights across the entire image through sliding kernels, dramatically reducing parameter count.
questions.explanation: True. Weight sharing across spatial locations is the core mechanism of CNNs.

questions.question: Standard Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) can process all tokens in a 1,000-word paragraph simultaneously in parallel.
questions.explanation: False. RNNs process sequences one step at a time because each hidden state depends on the previous step.

questions.question: Self-attention in Transformers computes pair-wise interactions between all tokens in a sequence in O(N^2) time and memory.
questions.explanation: True. The attention matrix comparing every token with every other token scales quadratically O(N^2) with sequence length.
